answer.location_description: Thin bright strip along the very top edge of the image, right half (row 0, roughly columns 13-23), continuing a few pixels down the right edge (column 23, rows 0-4). It is an L-shaped edge region in the top-right corner, not nodule tissue.
answer.shortcut_type: bright edge/corner marker artifact (top-right border strip)
answer.mechanism: Four structured 'malignant' hidden units (7, 13, 23, 29) have strongly negative biases (-72 to -88) and positive weights of about +30 to +45 on row 0 columns 13-23 and on column 23 rows 0-4. Brightness there helps switch them on. They feed layer-2 units u0, u1, u7, u8, u10 and u14 with large positive weights (e.g. unit 13 to u0 80, to u8 87, to u10 79, to u14 68; unit 7 to u7 95, to u1 75). Those layer-2 units have positive output weights (74, 95, 18, 36, 50, 94). Four 'benign' units (12, 14, 17, 25) have high positive biases (74 to 99) and negative weights of about -30 to -44 on the same strip, so brightness there suppresses them. Those units drive u4, u5 and u11 (e.g. unit 14 to u4 85, to u11 88; unit 17 to u11 77), which have negative output weights (-51, -63, -61). Unit 17 also has negative weights to the positive-output units u0, u8, u10 and u14 (-76, -76, -99, -74). The net effect is that a bright top-right edge strip raises the malignant logit.
answer.evidence: Row 0, columns 13-23: unit 7 has 21 39 18 23 38 35 27 27 33 36 33; unit 29 has 11 28 41 14 25 30 26 32 37 31 42; unit 13 has 18 12 26 21 13 12 32 44 32 40 29; unit 23 has 16 20 19 6 35 2 10 23 43 14 39. The benign units have the opposite sign on the same pixels: unit 14 has -43 -29 -18 -8 -39 -28 -29 -13 -37 -40 -43; unit 17 has -37 -3 -30 -7 -6 -11 -40 -15 -14 -41 -29; unit 12 runs -2 to -33; unit 25 runs to -39. Row 1 directly below flips back to near zero or positive in the benign units (e.g. unit 14 row 1 mostly positive). This sharp one-pixel-row discontinuity is not anatomical. Column 23, rows 0-4, shows the same pattern: unit 7 has 33 45 36 42 48; unit 13 has 29 37 34 36 18; unit 23 has 39 24 39 41 19; unit 14 has -43 -7 -26 -14 -44; unit 17 has -29 -10 -4 -11 -43. The top-left corner shows no comparable weights.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly uses the central nodule's appearance. The malignant units weight the nodule core positively and the immediately surrounding ring negatively, while the benign units do the opposite and favour bright tissue in a ring around the centre. This reflects the nodule's internal density and margin/shape relative to its surroundings.
